lead: No natural product has grade A evidence in insomnia. For melatonin, meta-analyses in insomnia and other primary sleep disorders found people fell asleep about 6 to 7 minutes sooner than with placebo, but a 2022 meta-analysis found no significant effect in adults with chronic insomnia (grade B). Valerian, magnesium, ashwagandha, probiotics, passionflower and saffron also have randomized trials with mixed, small or low-certainty results (grade B).

grade_key.A: Meta-analysis, or at least 2 randomized trials with low risk of bias and a consistent benefit
grade_key.B: 1 good randomized trial, or several randomized trials with mixed results
grade_key.C: Observational studies, small pilots or open-label trials only
grade_key.Negative: Randomized trials found no benefit over placebo

disclaimer: This page summarizes published research. It is not medical advice. Talk to a clinician before starting any supplement, especially if you take other medicines.

products.name: Ashwagandha
products.summary: A 2021 meta-analysis of 5 randomized trials in 400 adults found a small but significant effect of ashwagandha extract on overall sleep compared with placebo, more prominent in adults diagnosed with insomnia; results varied between trials. A 2024 meta-analysis of 5 randomized trials in 254 people with anxiety or insomnia found improvements in time to fall asleep, total sleep time and sleep-quality scores, but not in time awake during the night, and called for larger trials. In one randomized, double-blind trial, 60 people with insomnia took 300 mg of root extract or placebo twice daily for 10 weeks; time to fall asleep was significantly shorter with ashwagandha than with placebo at the end.
products.safety_interactions: The 2021 meta-analysis reported no serious side effects, but said that data on serious adverse effects are limited and that more safety data are needed to judge long-term use. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Ashwagandha
general_safety.short: Case reports link ashwagandha to liver injury (jaundice, itching), with deaths in people who already had cirrhosis, and to thyrotoxicosis in one reported case.

products.name: Kava
products.summary: Results are mixed, and kava has reports of liver injury (see safety). In a multicentre randomized, double-blind trial, 61 people with sleep disturbances linked to anxiety took 200 mg of a kava extract or placebo daily for 4 weeks; sleep quality and feeling restored after sleep improved more with kava. A 2015 meta-analysis of herbal medicines for insomnia, which included kava, found no significant difference between any herb and placebo. A randomized trial that assigned 391 people with anxiety and insomnia to three groups (121 to kava, 135 to valerian and 135 to placebo) concluded that kava did not relieve anxiety or insomnia more than placebo. A pilot study in 24 people with stress-induced insomnia reported improvement in insomnia during 6 weeks of kava; its abstract describes no placebo group.
products.safety_interactions: Kava has been linked to liver injury. A clinical review reports that ethanolic and acetonic kava extracts were banned in Germany in 2002 after reports connecting liver disease with kava, and that one positive re-exposure test confirmed that kava is potentially hepatotoxic (able to injure the liver). In 14 patients with liver disease assessed for causality, risk factors included overdose, prolonged treatment and taking other drugs or supplements at the same time. A second review notes numerous reports of severe liver toxicity potentially induced by kava in the USA and Europe. In the 61-person trial there were no drug-related adverse events or changes in laboratory values over 4 weeks, and the pilot study reported dizziness with kava.

general_safety.name: Kava
general_safety.short: Case reports describe rare but serious liver damage, plus skin and neurological reactions. Trial adverse events were mostly mild; a possible interaction with benzodiazepines has been reported.

products.name: Lavender oil (inhaled)
products.summary: A 2026 meta-analysis pooled 15 randomized trials of inhaled lavender oil in adults with primary sleep disorders or sleep disturbance linked to another condition. Sleep-quality scores improved more with lavender than with control, but results varied widely between trials, a statistical test suggested possible publication bias, and the authors said the findings should be interpreted cautiously. A 2025 review of 10 clinical trials in adults over 60 with sleep disorders, all using inhaled lavender, found improvement in 9 of them.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials. The 2025 review said more research is needed on safety, especially with long-term use.

general_safety.name: Lavender
general_safety.short: A large review found a safe profile in trials but poor safety reporting. Case reports link continuous use of lavender-fragranced products to breast growth in young children, reversing on stopping.

products.name: Magnesium
products.summary: A 2021 meta-analysis found 3 randomized trials comparing oral magnesium with placebo in 151 older adults with insomnia. People taking magnesium fell asleep about 17 minutes sooner; total sleep time did not differ significantly. All three trials were at moderate-to-high risk of bias and the evidence was rated low to very low quality. A double-blind randomized trial in 46 older adults tested 500 mg of magnesium or placebo daily for 8 weeks and found lower insomnia severity scores with magnesium. A randomized trial in 155 adults who reported poor sleep (not diagnosed insomnia) tested 250 mg of elemental magnesium daily as magnesium bisglycinate and found a slightly greater drop in insomnia severity scores than with placebo at 4 weeks, with a small effect size. A 2026 systematic review of 12 randomized trials found inconsistent results and concluded that current evidence does not support oral magnesium as a routine treatment for insomnia, with low or very low certainty.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Magnesium
general_safety.short: Oral magnesium mainly causes gastrointestinal effects such as diarrhoea; severe high blood magnesium occurs almost only in people with substantially reduced kidney function.

products.name: Melatonin
products.summary: Results are mixed. A 2013 meta-analysis of 19 placebo-controlled trials in 1683 adults and children with primary sleep disorders found that melatonin shortened the time to fall asleep by about 7 minutes and lengthened total sleep by about 8 minutes; the authors called the effects modest. A 2023 meta-analysis of 22 studies of melatonin or the prescription medicine ramelteon in insomnia disorder, in which 925 people received melatonin, found that prolonged-release melatonin shortened self-reported time to fall asleep by about 6 minutes compared with placebo. A 2022 meta-analysis of 24 randomized trials in chronic insomnia found no significant effect in adults on time to fall asleep, total sleep time or sleep efficiency. A 2017 American sleep medicine guideline suggested that clinicians not use melatonin for chronic insomnia in adults (a weak recommendation).
products.safety_interactions: A systematic review of 37 randomized trials of melatonin for sleep disorders found that the most frequently reported adverse events were daytime sleepiness (1.66%), headache (0.74%) and dizziness (0.74%); few were serious. The reviewers noted that most trials lasted 4 weeks or less, which limits conclusions about long-term use. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Melatonin
general_safety.short: Trial adverse events were few and mostly mild (daytime sleepiness, headache, dizziness); long-term data are limited. Drugs acting on CYP1A2 may slow its breakdown.

products.name: Passionflower
products.summary: In a double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial in 110 adults with insomnia disorder, 2 weeks of passionflower extract increased total sleep time measured in the sleep laboratory compared with placebo (P = 0.049). Sleep efficiency and time awake during the night improved in the passionflower group but did not differ from placebo. A second randomized, double-blind trial in 65 people with stress and insomnia found longer total sleep time with a passionflower extract than with placebo over 30 days. A trial of passionflower tea found better sleep-quality ratings than with placebo tea, but it studied 41 healthy adults, not people with insomnia.
products.safety_interactions: The 65-person trial reported no adverse effects with the extract. The other cited abstracts do not report safety data. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Passionflower
general_safety.short: A systematic review of nine short clinical trials (up to 30 days) observed no adverse effects. In one small trial, job-performance impairment was less common than with oxazepam.

products.name: Probiotics
products.summary: A 2025 meta-analysis of 6 randomized trials in 424 people with insomnia found that probiotics lowered (improved) a standard sleep-quality score by about 2 points compared with control, rated moderate certainty. There was no significant effect on total sleep time or sleep efficiency, and the authors said the sample was limited. A 2026 meta-analysis of 39 placebo-controlled trials in 4094 adults and adolescents, not limited to people with insomnia, found a small improvement in sleep-quality scores (very low certainty) and no overall improvement in insomnia severity.
products.safety_interactions: The 2025 meta-analysis found no significant difference in total adverse events between probiotic and control groups. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Probiotics
general_safety.short: Trials have not shown increased risk, though safety reporting is weak. Rare bloodstream infections occur, mainly in people who are severely ill, immunosuppressed or in intensive care.

products.name: Saffron
products.summary: A 2022 meta-analysis of 8 articles with 431 participants found better sleep quality with saffron than with placebo (very low-quality evidence) and longer sleep duration (moderate-quality evidence). The pooled difference in insomnia severity favoured saffron but was not statistically significant (p = 0.08). A second 2022 meta-analysis of randomized trials found lower (better) sleep-quality scores with saffron than with placebo; it pooled healthy adults with people who had insomnia, type 2 diabetes or were on methadone maintenance treatment, so it is not limited to insomnia.
products.safety_interactions: One meta-analysis reported that no serious adverse events occurred as the dose was increased, and said long-term safety needs further study. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Saffron
general_safety.short: In a meta-analysis of 12 depression studies, adverse effects were no more common than with placebo. In a 1-week volunteer study the higher dose lowered standing blood pressure.

products.name: Suanzaoren (sour jujube seed)
products.summary: A 2023 meta-analysis included 9 randomized trials with 785 people with insomnia disorder and 120 with sleep disturbance. Compared with placebo, suanzaoren improved self-reported sleep quality in the short term; the placebo-controlled studies had a low risk of bias. Longer-term results were mixed, and the authors said the benefits and harms need testing in a larger trial because of small samples and variable study quality.
products.safety_interactions: The meta-analysis reported that suanzaoren did not increase the incidence of major adverse events. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited study.

general_safety.name: Sour jujube seed (suanzaoren)
general_safety.short: In a meta-analysis of 9 randomised trials, suanzaoren did not increase major adverse events; the authors said harms, particularly long term, need further study.

citations.label: Yang et al., 2023, Integr Cancer Ther
citations.title: The Herbal Medicine Suanzaoren (Ziziphi Spinosae Semen) for Sleep Quality Improvements: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

products.name: Valerian
products.summary: Results are mixed and lean towards little measurable effect. A 2010 meta-analysis of 18 randomized placebo-controlled trials found that people taking valerian were more likely to say their sleep had improved (relative risk 1.37), but the time to fall asleep differed from placebo by less than a minute and sleep-quality scores did not differ. A 2006 meta-analysis of 16 trials in 1093 people found a similar yes-or-no benefit, with evidence of publication bias and methodological problems in most studies. A 2015 meta-analysis of herbal medicines in 1602 people with insomnia found no significant difference between any herb, including valerian, and placebo. In a randomized trial run over the internet, 391 people with anxiety and insomnia were assigned to three groups; the 135 given valerian and the 135 given placebo had similar improvements in sleep over 4 weeks. A 2024 randomized trial in 80 adults with sleep complaints found better sleep-quality scores with a valerian extract than with placebo over 8 weeks. A 2017 American sleep medicine guideline suggested that clinicians not use valerian for chronic insomnia (a weak recommendation).
products.safety_interactions: Reports differ. A 2015 meta-analysis of insomnia trials found more adverse events per person with valerian than with placebo. A 2007 systematic review described valerian as associated with only rare adverse events, and the 2024 trial reported no safety concerns. In a pilot study, vivid dreams were the most common effect reported with valerian (16% of 19 people). Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Valerian
general_safety.short: No severe adverse events in a review of 60 studies (6,894 people). An interaction review found low interaction potential. A case report describes valerian-associated liver toxicity.

products.name: Valerian with hops
products.summary: In a multicentre randomized placebo-controlled trial in 184 adults with mild insomnia, a valerian-hops combination taken for 28 days gave modest improvements in self-reported sleep, but few comparisons with placebo reached statistical significance and no sleep measure recorded in the sleep laboratory differed between groups. People taking the combination rated their insomnia as less severe than those on placebo after 14 days. A randomized, double-blind feasibility trial in 40 people with occasional sleep problems found about 22 minutes more sleep a night with a valerian-hops extract than with placebo in exploratory analyses.
products.safety_interactions: In the 184-person trial there were no serious adverse events, no significant residual effects and no rebound insomnia after stopping. The feasibility trial described the product as well tolerated. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Valerian
general_safety.short: No severe adverse events in a review of 60 studies (6,894 people). An interaction review found low interaction potential. A case report describes valerian-associated liver toxicity.

general_safety.name: Hops
general_safety.short: No related adverse events in a 12-week trial of a matured hop extract; a valerian-hops combination was well tolerated. A 19-man study of hop extract reported nausea, bloating and abdominal discomfort.

products.name: Cannabidiol (CBD)
products.summary: In a randomized, placebo-controlled pilot trial in 30 people with primary insomnia, 150 mg of CBD nightly for 2 weeks did not differ from placebo in insomnia severity, self-reported time to fall asleep, sleep efficiency or time awake during the night; objectively measured sleep efficiency was better with CBD after 2 weeks. In a double-blind, randomized crossover trial in 125 people with insomnia, 300 mg of CBD with added terpenes marginally increased the share of the night spent in deep and REM sleep, measured by a wrist-worn tracker, and had no effect on total sleep time. A 2023 systematic review found that only 2 of 34 studies of CBD and sleep focused on people with insomnia, and one of those was a case report. Graded C because the placebo-controlled trials in insomnia are small or showed little effect on insomnia symptoms.
products.safety_interactions: In the 30-person trial, people taking CBD were more likely than those on placebo to report dry mouth, and daytime cognitive performance was unaffected. The 125-person trial reported no adverse events. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Cannabidiol (CBD)
general_safety.short: Raises the chance of liver enzyme elevation, especially at high doses or with antiseizure drugs. Raises a clobazam metabolite and may interact with drugs using CYP450 enzymes.

products.name: Cannabis oil (THC with CBD)
products.summary: One randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial tested an oil containing 10 mg/ml THC and 15 mg/ml CBD for 2 weeks; 29 people with self-reported clinical insomnia completed it. After the cannabis oil period, 60% no longer met the questionnaire threshold for clinical insomnia, and light sleep measured by a wrist tracker increased by 21 minutes a night compared with placebo. The authors noted that effects were more pronounced in the second phase because of a period effect and loss of blinding. Graded C because this is a single small trial in which blinding was lost.
products.safety_interactions: The trial described the oil as generally well tolerated; the abstract does not list adverse events. The oil tested contains THC. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trial.

general_safety.name: THC-containing cannabis and cannabinoids
general_safety.short: Trials show more short-term adverse events, including dizziness, drowsiness, confusion and hallucinations, and more withdrawals due to adverse events than placebo.

general_safety.name: Cannabidiol (CBD)
general_safety.short: Raises the chance of liver enzyme elevation, especially at high doses or with antiseizure drugs. Raises a clobazam metabolite and may interact with drugs using CYP450 enzymes.

products.name: Chamomile oil (inhaled)
products.summary: In one randomized trial, 80 adults aged 18 to 35 with insomnia either inhaled chamomile oil for 10 minutes a day for 15 days or carried on with their normal routine. Sleep-quality and insomnia severity scores were better in the chamomile group afterwards. There was no placebo or other active comparison, and the authors said the result needs repeating against an active control. Graded C because the trial was not placebo-controlled.
products.safety_interactions: No participant in either group reported adverse events during or after the study. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trial.

general_safety.name: Chamomile
general_safety.short: Only mild adverse events in a review of 12 trials. A warfarin review lists chamomile tea among items with increased bleeding risk; a case report describes anaphylaxis to chamomile tea.

citations.label: Deepa et al., 2025, Int J Psychiatry Med
citations.title: Effects of chamomile oil inhalation on sleep quality in young adults with insomnia: A randomized controlled trial.

products.name: L-tryptophan
products.summary: The trials in insomnia are small and old. In a double-blind crossover study in 39 people with chronic insomnia, 2 g of L-tryptophan was better than a very low comparison dose only in the group that took the full dose first. In a double-blind placebo-controlled study in which 49 of 57 people with chronic insomnia finished, a tryptophan-rich protein source with carbohydrate and pharmaceutical-grade tryptophan with carbohydrate improved insomnia measures, while carbohydrate alone did not. A 2022 meta-analysis pooling 4 articles found that tryptophan shortened time awake during the night but did not affect other sleep measures; its abstract does not say the participants had insomnia. A 2017 American sleep medicine guideline suggested that clinicians not use tryptophan for chronic insomnia (a weak recommendation). Graded C rather than B because the insomnia trials are small and their results are inconsistent.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Tryptophan
general_safety.short: Occasional tremor, nausea and dizziness, mainly at higher doses; rare serotonin syndrome with serotonergic medicines. A 1989 eosinophilia-myalgia outbreak was linked to contaminated supplements.

products.name: Lemon balm
products.summary: One double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study of a lemon balm extract reported lower insomnia severity scores with the extract than with placebo (6.8 against 9.7 points); its abstract does not give the number of participants or say whether they had diagnosed insomnia. A separate placebo-controlled trial in 100 women aged 50 to 60 with sleep complaints during menopause found better sleep-quality scores with a combination of valerian and lemon balm, which cannot show the effect of lemon balm alone. Graded C because the evidence for lemon balm alone is a single study with limited reporting.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Lemon balm
general_safety.short: Two meta-analyses of randomised trials (anxiety and depression; cardiometabolic outcomes) reported no serious side effects, but the trials were few and often at high risk of bias.

products.name: Tart cherry juice
products.summary: Two very small crossover pilot studies tested tart cherry juice in older adults with insomnia. In a randomized, double-blind crossover study in 15 people, 2 weeks of a tart cherry juice blend reduced minutes awake during the night compared with a placebo drink, with no difference in time to fall asleep, total sleep time or sleep efficiency; the authors noted the effects were considerably smaller than those of hypnotic medicines and cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia. In a placebo-controlled crossover study, the 8 people who finished slept 84 minutes longer in the sleep laboratory after 2 weeks of cherry juice (240 mL twice a day); most questionnaires showed no difference.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Tart cherry
general_safety.short: In a 28-day trial in 50 people with gout, only 1 of 24 adverse events (high blood sugar) was judged possibly related. In a knee osteoarthritis trial, withdrawals were similar to placebo.

products.name: Chamomile (oral)
products.summary: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial in 34 adults with chronic primary insomnia tested 270 mg of chamomile extract or placebo twice daily for 28 days. There were no significant differences between groups in any sleep diary measure. A 2019 meta-analysis reported that only one randomized trial had tested chamomile for insomnia and that it found no significant change in insomnia severity. Meta-analyses that pooled trials in healthy adults and people with other conditions report better sleep-quality scores with chamomile, but that is not evidence in insomnia. Graded Negative because the only randomized trial in insomnia found no significant differences from placebo; this rests on a single small pilot trial.
products.safety_interactions: In the insomnia pilot trial, adverse events did not differ between chamomile and placebo. A 2024 meta-analysis found no adverse events reported in its included studies, though most relied on participants volunteering them. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Chamomile
general_safety.short: Only mild adverse events in a review of 12 trials. A warfarin review lists chamomile tea among items with increased bleeding risk; a case report describes anaphylaxis to chamomile tea.

citations.title: Effects of chamomile (Matricaria chamomilla L.) on sleep: A systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical trials.

products.name: 5-HTP (5-hydroxytryptophan)
products.summary: No trial of 5-HTP in people with diagnosed insomnia was found in a PubMed search on 25 November 2026. One single-blinded randomized trial assigned 30 older adults to take 100 mg of 5-HTP daily for 12 weeks or nothing; there was no placebo. The authors reported improvement in some sleep-quality components, seen mainly in those who were poor sleepers at the start. The participants were not selected for insomnia, so this is too little to judge.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: 5-HTP (5-hydroxytryptophan)
general_safety.short: A safety review found no definitive toxicity cases in 20 years of use; a link to eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome is unresolved. One case report of serotonin syndrome with linezolid.

citations.title: The impact of 5-hydroxytryptophan supplementation on sleep quality and gut microbiota composition in older adults: A randomized controlled trial.

products.name: Cannabinol (CBN)
products.summary: One randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial tested single doses of 30 mg and 300 mg of cannabinol for one night each in 20 adults with physician-diagnosed insomnia disorder. Cannabinol did not significantly change the main outcome, minutes awake during the night measured in the sleep laboratory. The 300 mg dose shortened time to fall asleep and improved self-rated sleep quality, which were secondary outcomes. A single-night trial in 20 people is too little to judge.
products.safety_interactions: The trial recorded 247 mild-to-moderate adverse events across its three arms, including placebo; the abstract does not break them down. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trial.

general_safety.name: Cannabinol (CBN)
general_safety.short: Human safety data are very limited: one single-night trial in 20 adults recorded 247 mild-to-moderate adverse events across all arms, including placebo. No interaction data were found.

citations.label: Lavender et al., 2026, J Sleep Res
citations.title: Cannabinol for Acute Treatment of Insomnia Disorder in a Randomized Placebo-Controlled Crossover Trial.

products.name: Ginkgo biloba
products.summary: No randomized or observational studies of ginkgo biloba in people with insomnia were found in PubMed searches on 25 November 2026.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials, because no insomnia trials of ginkgo biloba were found.

general_safety.name: Ginkgo biloba
general_safety.short: Trials of clotting measures indicate no higher bleeding risk, but case reports describe bleeding, including intracranial. Interactions with anticoagulant or antiplatelet medicines cannot be ruled out.

products.name: Glycine
products.summary: No trial of glycine in people with diagnosed insomnia was found in PubMed searches on 25 November 2026. A 2012 review by the researchers who study glycine states that taking it before bedtime improved self-rated sleep quality in people with insomniac tendencies, but the original trial reports were not found in PubMed and could not be checked. A study by the same group gave 3 g of glycine or placebo before bedtime to healthy volunteers whose sleep was deliberately restricted and found less next-day fatigue; that is not a study of insomnia.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Glycine
general_safety.short: In a randomised trial in 214 heart patients, side effects with long-term oral glycine were similar to placebo. A small schizophrenia study found antipsychotic blood levels were not altered.

citations.label: Bannai et al., 2012, J Pharmacol Sci
citations.title: New therapeutic strategy for amino acid medicine: glycine improves the quality of sleep.

citations.label: Bannai et al., 2012, Front Neurol
citations.title: The effects of glycine on subjective daytime performance in partially sleep-restricted healthy volunteers.

products.name: L-theanine
products.summary: No meta-analysis or trial limited to people with diagnosed insomnia was found in a PubMed search on 25 November 2026. A 2025 meta-analysis of 18 randomized trials pooled people of all ages and health status and found small improvements in self-reported time to fall asleep, daytime functioning and overall sleep quality; the authors noted a lack of studies of L-theanine on its own. A 2026 systematic review of 13 trials of L-theanine alone reported benefits on sleep measures in adults and said trials in people with clinical insomnia are still needed. This evidence is about sleep quality in general, so it is too little to judge an effect on insomnia.
products.safety_interactions: The 2026 systematic review described L-theanine supplementation as appearing safe in adults; the cited abstracts do not list adverse events. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: L-theanine
general_safety.short: In a meta-analysis of 31 randomised trials (1168 people), no serious adverse events were reported. Small add-on trials with sertraline or risperidone found side effects similar to placebo.

citations.label: Bulman et al., 2025, Sleep Med Rev
citations.title: The effects of L-theanine consumption on sleep outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

citations.label: Cotter et al., 2026, Nutr Neurosci
citations.title: Examining the effect of L-theanine on sleep: a systematic review of dietary supplementation trials.

products.name: Lavender oil (oral capsules)
products.summary: No trial of oral lavender oil in people with diagnosed insomnia was found in a PubMed search on 25 November 2026. One randomized, double-blind trial tested 80 mg of an oral lavender oil preparation once daily for 10 weeks in 170 outpatients with anxiety-related restlessness and disturbed sleep. Anxiety scores fell more than with placebo. A sleep-quality questionnaire was among the outcomes, and the abstract says the effect was more pronounced than with placebo on all outcome measures, but it gives no separate sleep result. This is too little to judge an effect on insomnia.
products.safety_interactions: Adverse events were reported by 33.7% of participants taking the lavender preparation and 35.7% taking placebo. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trial.

general_safety.name: Lavender
general_safety.short: A large review found a safe profile in trials but poor safety reporting. Case reports link continuous use of lavender-fragranced products to breast growth in young children, reversing on stopping.

citations.label: Kasper et al., 2015, Eur Neuropsychopharmacol
citations.title: Efficacy of orally administered Silexan in patients with anxiety-related restlessness and disturbed sleep--A randomized, placebo-controlled trial.

products.name: Vitamin D
products.summary: No meta-analysis or trial of vitamin D limited to people with diagnosed insomnia was found in a PubMed search on 25 November 2026. Two 2022 meta-analyses of supplementation studies, not limited to people with insomnia, found better sleep-quality scores with vitamin D than with placebo or control. One of them concluded that results for sleep disorders were not unanimous and that the effect on sleep quantity and sleep disorders needs more study.
products.safety_interactions: One of the meta-analyses reported that vitamin D supplementation did not cause any side effects in its included trials. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Vitamin D
general_safety.short: Long-term supplementation raised the risk of high blood calcium and high urine calcium in trials, but not kidney stones; toxicity from extremely high doses is rare but serious.
